---
title: "Using Q-CRAFT from Python"
subtitle: "A practical guide for macro-fiscal and climate-risk analysis"
---

Q-CRAFT (2024-11-15) is a Python reimplementation of the Q-CRAFT workbook. It combines country data with assumptions about demography, labour productivity, inflation, and interest rates to produce a baseline through 2099. Climate scenarios then alter the growth path and fiscal position.

This site documents the generated Python package, whose public interface is in `qcraft.api`. It is intended for economists who want a reproducible, scriptable counterpart to the Q-CRAFT Excel workbook. Results are conditional scenarios, not forecasts.

## Installation

Install the package directly from GitHub:

```bash
uv add "qcraft-2024-11-15 @ git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/qcraft-2024-11-15"
```

Import public calculations from `qcraft.api`:

```{python}
from qcraft import BaselinePopulationGrowthInputs
from qcraft.api import compute_baseline_population_growth

result = compute_baseline_population_growth(BaselinePopulationGrowthInputs(
    country="France",
    demography_scenario="Medium",
))
result.domain.axes[0].keys[0], result.domain.axes[0].keys[-1], result[2099]
```

Each public function accepts one explicit `*Inputs` object. The input classes and calculation functions are re-exported from `qcraft`; calculation functions themselves are available from `qcraft.api`. Annual results are immutable named-axis `Series` objects: use `.domain.axes` to inspect their keys, `.items()` to iterate coordinate/value pairs, and `.sel(...)` to select a scenario. This preserves year and scenario identity instead of relying on positional tuple indices.

## What the results mean

Q-CRAFT is a partial-equilibrium scenario tool, not a forecast or a general-equilibrium model. Its results are conditional on the assumptions supplied by the analyst. The baseline uses a simple production relationship and debt dynamics; climate scenarios apply empirical GDP effects and then trace their fiscal consequences.

Use the results to:

- compare the direction and scale of long-term fiscal pressures;
- identify sensitivity to demographic, productivity, inflation, and interest-rate assumptions;
- quantify the additional fiscal task associated with climate scenarios; and
- identify questions that require a country-specific model or granular sectoral analysis.

The package does not endogenise adaptation spending, natural-disaster GDP losses, sea-level rise, monetary conditions, external balances, or the GDP effects of fiscal consolidation. Discrete revenue and expenditure shocks can be entered separately, but their GDP effects are not modelled.
